entities.summary:
Adriano Tessarollo (born 1950) is an Italian Catholic bishop who has served as Bishop of Chioggia in the Veneto region. His episcopate in one of Venice's satellite dioceses situates him within the rich Catholic culture of northeastern Italy — a region marked by deep popular piety, strong Catholic institutional networks, and the influence of the Patriarchate of Venice as one of Italy's most historically significant sees.

The Veneto region's Catholicism has been notable for its resistance to secularisation compared to other parts of northern Italy, maintaining higher rates of religious practice and strong parish community life. Bishops like Tessarollo serve in an environment where the Church's social role — in education, healthcare, charitable work — remains substantial and where the episcopal office carries genuine public significance.

His episcopate at Chioggia reflects the Italian Church's commitment to maintaining strong local episcopal leadership in every diocese, however small, as part of the apostolic tradition. His work in the pastoral care of a fishing community and industrial port city demonstrates the range of social contexts within which Italian Catholic bishops exercise their ministry.
